title: x86-64 page table entry (PTE)
summary: An x86-64 page table entry (PTE) is 8 bytes (64 bits). For a 4-level paging (PML4 -> PDPT -> PD -> PT), each entry: bit 0 = Present (P), bit 1 = Read/Write (R/W), bit 2 = User/Supervisor (U/S), bit 3 = Write-Through (PWT), bit 4 = Cache Disable (PCD), bit 5 = Accessed (A), bit 6 = Dirty (D, only for leaf entries), bit 7 = Page Size (PS, for large pages), bits 8 = Global (G), bits 9-11 = Available (for OS use), bits 12-51 = Physical Frame Number (PFN), bits 52-58 = Available (for OS use), bit 59 = Protection Key (PK), bit 60 = Execute Disable (XD/NX).

ext.summary: An x86-64 page table entry (PTE) is 8 bytes (64 bits). For a 4-level paging (PML4 -> PDPT -> PD -> PT), each entry: bit 0 = Present (P), bit 1 = Read/Write (R/W), bit 2 = User/Supervisor (U/S), bit 3 = Write-Through (PWT), bit 4 = Cache Disable (PCD), bit 5 = Accessed (A), bit 6 = Dirty (D, only for leaf entries), bit 7 = Page Size (PS, for large pages), bits 8 = Global (G), bits 9-11 = Available (for OS use), bits 12-51 = Physical Frame Number (PFN), bits 52-58 = Available (for OS use), bit 59 = Protection Key (PK), bit 60 = Execute Disable (XD/NX).

structure.meaning: 1 = page is present in memory. 0 = not present (page fault on access).
0 = read-only, 1 = read/write. Only effective if CR0.WP=1 for supervisor.
Set by hardware on read/write. Used by OS for page replacement.
Set by hardware on write. Only for leaf (PT) entries.
1 = large page (2MB in PD, 1GB in PDPT). Only for non-leaf entries.
1 = global page (not flushed on CR3 reload). Requires CR4.PGE=1.
Physical page frame number (address bits 12-51). Page size determines alignment.
Available for OS use (if not using protection keys).

notes: x86-64 uses 4-level paging (PML4 -> PDPT -> PD -> PT) by default, or 5-level with LA57.
Page sizes: 4KB (PT), 2MB (PD with PS=1), 1GB (PDPT with PS=1).
CR3 holds the physical address of the PML4 table.
TLB caches recent translations; INVLPG invalidates a single entry.
PCID (Process-Context Identifier) avoids TLB flushes on context switch.
